overall_assessment: Design is sound for v1 scope but has significant gaps for the <200ms p95 NFR at 10k models. Current spec omits critical performance infrastructure (indexes, caching, pagination strategy, connection pool sizing). Achievable with targeted additions.

current_design_issues: No explicit indexes defined in spec for query patterns (category, provider, modality, status, slug)
Offset-based pagination (page/page_size) will degrade linearly beyond page ~50
No caching layer specified for read-heavy public endpoints
N+1 risk: model response includes provider + categories + translations = 3+ joins per item
Full-text search using PostgreSQL ILIKE on unindexed columns will scan entire table
No materialized views or denormalization for common query shapes
required_changes: Add composite indexes: (status, category_id), (status, provider_id), (status, modality), (slug)
Implement keyset pagination for list endpoints
Add Redis cache layer with TTL for public read endpoints
Use SELECT ... JOIN with subqueries or lateral joins to fetch provider + categories + translations in single query
Implement PostgreSQL tsvector + GIN index for full-text search
Consider materialized view for 'approved models with translations' refreshed on approval
1_nfr_200ms_p95_10k_models.estimated_latency_with_fixes: 50-150ms p95 at 10k models on modest hardware (2 vCPU, 4GB RAM)

2_query_patterns_indexing_strategy.current_state: No indexes specified in spec. Only PKs and unique constraints implied.
query_patterns_from_spec: GET /models?modality=text,code&status=approved → filter by modality array + status
GET /models?q=search → full-text on slug, display_name, family
GET /models/{slug} → PK lookup + translations + categories + provider
recommended_indexes: CREATE INDEX idx_aimodel_status_category ON ai_model (status, category_id) WHERE status = 'approved'
CREATE INDEX idx_aimodel_status_provider ON ai_model (status, provider_id) WHERE status = 'approved'
CREATE INDEX idx_aimodel_status_modality ON ai_model (status, modality) WHERE status = 'approved' USING GIN
CREATE INDEX idx_aimodel_search_tsv ON ai_model USING GIN (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(slug,'') || ' ' || coalesce(display_name,'') || ' ' || coalesce(family,''))) WHERE status = 'approved'
CREATE INDEX idx_category_version_status ON category (taxonomy_version, status) WHERE status = 'active'
CREATE INDEX idx_category_translation_lookup ON category_translation (category_id, locale)
CREATE INDEX idx_model_translation_lookup ON model_translation (model_id, locale)
2_query_patterns_indexing_strategy.partial_index_rationale: Public API only queries approved models. Partial indexes reduce size ~80% and speed up writes.

3_pagination_offset_vs_keyset.current_spec: Uses page (int, default 1) + page_size (int, default 20, max 100) — OFFSET pagination
3_pagination_offset_vs_keyset.problem: OFFSET requires scanning and discarding N rows. At 10k models with page_size=20, page 500 = 10k rows scanned. Latency grows O(N). Unacceptable for p95 <200ms.
3_pagination_offset_vs_keyset.recommendation: Switch to keyset (cursor) pagination for public list endpoints

implementation.query_pattern: WHERE (display_name, id) > (?, ?) ORDER BY display_name, id LIMIT 21
implementation.response_change: Replace page/page_size with cursor + limit. Return next_cursor or null.
implementation.backward_compatibility: Support both for transition; deprecate offset after v1

3_pagination_offset_vs_keyset.tradeoff: Keyset prevents random page access but provides consistent <10ms latency at any depth. Acceptable for infinite scroll / next-page UX.

4_full_text_search_implementation.current_spec: GET /models?q=claude — 'Full-text search on slug, display_name, family' using ILIKE implied
4_full_text_search_implementation.problem: ILIKE '%query%' cannot use standard B-tree indexes. Sequential scan on 10k rows = 50-200ms. No ranking, no stemming, no typo tolerance.
4_full_text_search_implementation.recommendation: PostgreSQL built-in full-text search with tsvector + GIN index

implementation.add_column: search_vector tsvector GENERATED ALWAYS AS (to_tsvector('simple', coalesce(slug,'') || ' ' || coalesce(display_name,'') || ' ' || coalesce(family,''))) STORED
implementation.index: CREATE INDEX idx_aimodel_search ON ai_model USING GIN (search_vector) WHERE status = 'approved'
implementation.query: SELECT * FROM ai_model WHERE search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('simple', $1) AND status = 'approved' ORDER BY ts_rank_cd(search_vector, plainto_tsquery('simple', $1)) DESC LIMIT 20
implementation.benefits: Sub-10ms at 100k rows, ranking, stemming, prefix matching via to_tsquery
implementation.alternative_for_v2: Meilisearch/Typesense if fuzzy search, faceting, or analytics needed

5_caching_strategy_redis.current_spec: Redis URL configured but no caching strategy documented
gaps: No invalidation on model approval/category changes
No handling of i18n variations (5 locales × query params = cache explosion risk)
5_caching_strategy_redis.recommendation: Cache public read endpoints with structured keys and targeted invalidation

cache_design.ttl: 300s (5 min) for lists, 3600s (1h) for detail, 86400s (24h) for categories/providers
cache_design.invalidation: On model approve/reject: DEL taxonomy:v1:models:* (pattern). On category change: DEL taxonomy:v1:categories:*. On taxonomy version activate: FLUSHDB taxonomy:v1:*
cache_design.i18n_optimization: Cache translated responses per locale. 5 locales × ~20 common filter combos = ~100 keys. Acceptable.
cache_design.cache_stampede: Use SETNX + short TTL lock for rebuild, or probabilistic early expiration

5_caching_strategy_redis.redis_sizing: 10k models × ~2KB serialized × 5 locales × 2 (list+detail) ≈ 200MB. Well within single Redis instance.

6_n1_risks_in_api_responses.current_spec: Model list response includes provider object, categories array, translations — implies N+1 if implemented naively
6_n1_risks_in_api_responses.naive_orm_pattern: for model in models: model.provider, model.categories, model.translations → 1 + 3N queries
recommended_patterns: Single query with JOINs + lateral subqueries for translations/categories
Or: fetch models → collect IDs → batch fetch providers + categories + translations in 3 queries
Or: SQLAlchemy selectinload for provider, categories; joinedload for translations
Response shape must match spec — denormalize provider slug/name into model row to avoid join
6_n1_risks_in_api_responses.optimal_query: SELECT m.*, p.slug as provider_slug, p.name as provider_name, json_agg(DISTINCT ct.*) as translations, json_agg(DISTINCT c.slug) as category_slugs FROM ai_model m JOIN provider p ON m.provider_id = p.id LEFT JOIN LATERAL (SELECT * FROM model_translation WHERE model_id = m.id AND locale = $lang UNION ALL SELECT * FROM model_translation WHERE model_id = m.id AND locale = 'en' LIMIT 1) ct ON true LEFT JOIN model_category mc ON m.id = mc.model_id LEFT JOIN category c ON mc.category_id = c.id WHERE m.status = 'approved' AND (...) GROUP BY m.id, p.id ORDER BY ... LIMIT 21
6_n1_risks_in_api_responses.verification: Add integration test asserting query count = 1 for list endpoint

7_database_connection_pooling.assessment: Adequate for low-concurrency v1. Risky for production burst traffic.
7_database_connection_pooling.calculation: Assume 100 RPS peak, avg query 10ms → 1 concurrent connection per 100 RPS. pool=10 handles ~1000 RPS. But with asyncpg + FastAPI, each request holds connection for full request duration (~50-100ms). pool=10 supports ~100-200 concurrent requests.
recommendations: Increase pool_size to 20, max_overflow to 30 for production
Add PgBouncer in transaction mode for connection multiplexing (reduces backend connections 10x)
Monitor pool usage: log pool.checkedout() / pool.size() periodically
Set statement_timeout=5000 and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout=30000 on PostgreSQL

8_ingestion_performance_batch_upserts.current_spec: Idempotent ingestion from OpenRouter/HF/LMSYS. Per-model errors don't abort. Creates IngestionRun record.
performance_concerns: No batch size specified — row-by-row upsert = 1000s of round trips
Deduplication checks (3 strategies) require SELECT before INSERT/UPDATE
No transaction batching — each model in own transaction = slow
No COPY / bulk insert strategy for initial seed / large imports
recommendations: Use PostgreSQL INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (provider_id, slug) DO UPDATE for single-statement upsert
Batch size: 500-1000 rows per transaction
Stage raw source data in temp table → single MERGE/upsert into ai_model
Compute source_payload_hash in Python, pass as column
For 10k models: expect <30s with batched upserts vs >10min row-by-row
Add ingestion_metrics table for observability (rows/sec, errors/sec)
8_ingestion_performance_batch_upserts.sample_upsert: INSERT INTO ai_model (id, slug, provider_id, display_name, version, family, modality, context_window, max_output_tokens, input_price_per_mtok, output_price_per_mtok, release_date, deprecation_date, status, source, source_url, source_payload_hash) VALUES ... ON CONFLICT (provider_id, slug) DO UPDATE SET display_name=EXCLUDED.display_name, version=EXCLUDED.version, family=EXCLUDED.family, modality=EXCLUDED.modality, context_window=EXCLUDED.context_window, max_output_tokens=EXCLUDED.max_output_tokens, input_price_per_mtok=EXCLUDED.input_price_per_mtok, output_price_per_mtok=EXCLUDED.output_price_per_mtok, release_date=EXCLUDED.release_date, deprecation_date=EXCLUDED.deprecation_date, status=EXCLUDED.status, source=EXCLUDED.source, source_url=EXCLUDED.source_url, source_payload_hash=EXCLUDED.source_payload_hash, updated_at=now()

9_taxonomy_version_query_patterns.current_spec: Categories have taxonomy_version. Only one is_current. Public API uses current version.
query_patterns: Public: categories for current version → WHERE taxonomy_version = (SELECT version FROM taxonomy_version WHERE is_current)
Admin: list all versions → SELECT * FROM taxonomy_version
Historical: votes/comparisons reference version at creation time
performance_issues: Subquery for current version on every category query
Category queries don't filter by version in spec (UC3 shows ?lang=zh only)
recommendations: Add UNIQUE INDEX ON taxonomy_version (is_current) WHERE is_current = true (enforces single current)
Add index: CREATE INDEX idx_category_version ON category (taxonomy_version, status)
Cache current version ID in Redis (key: taxonomy:v1:current_version, TTL 1h, invalidate on activate)
Public category query: JOIN taxonomy_version tv ON c.taxonomy_version = tv.version WHERE tv.is_current AND c.status = 'active'
Denormalize is_current into category table (generated column or trigger) for partition pruning

10_cdn_edge_caching_public_endpoints.current_spec: No CDN/edge strategy documented. Public endpoints are read-only.
10_cdn_edge_caching_public_endpoints.opportunity: Public endpoints (models list, detail, categories, providers) are ideal for edge caching — immutable for approved data, vary by locale and filters
recommendations: Add Cache-Control headers: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300 for list endpoints
Detail endpoints: public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=3600
Categories/Providers: public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400
Vary header: Accept-Language, Accept (for JSON), or use query params in cache key
Use Cloudflare Workers / CloudFront Functions to serve from edge with cache tags
Cache tag invalidation: tag responses with 'taxonomy:models', 'taxonomy:categories'. On model approve: purge 'taxonomy:models'. On category change: purge 'taxonomy:categories'
Edge caching reduces origin load 90%+ for read-heavy workloads
caveats: Admin endpoints must bypass CDN (auth + Cache-Control: private, no-store)
Search endpoint (q=) should not be edge-cached (high cardinality)
Cursor pagination: each cursor is unique → cache per cursor or use page-based at edge

priority_1_blockers_for_nfr: Add partial indexes for approved models on (status, category_id), (status, provider_id), (status, modality), (slug), and tsvector GIN
Implement keyset pagination for GET /models and GET /categories
Add Redis cache layer with defined keys, TTLs, and invalidation on approval/category change
Fix N+1: implement single-query fetch with lateral joins or batch loading for provider/categories/translations
Implement PostgreSQL full-text search with tsvector + GIN index
priority_2_before_production: Increase DB pool to 20/30, add PgBouncer in transaction mode
Add statement_timeout and idle_in_transaction_session_timeout on PostgreSQL
Implement batched upsert with ON CONFLICT for ingestion (500-1000 rows/batch)
Add Cache-Control headers + CDN cache tags for public endpoints
Cache current taxonomy version in Redis with invalidation on activate
priority_3_v2_enhancements: Materialized view for 'approved models with translations' refreshed via trigger on approval
Meilisearch/Typesense for advanced search (facets, typo tolerance, analytics)
Partition ai_model by status (approved vs pending) for query isolation
Read replicas for public read endpoints
Async ingestion with background worker + progress polling

estimated_effort.priority_1: 2-3 days (indexes, pagination, cache, N+1 fix, FTS)
estimated_effort.priority_2: 1-2 days (pool, PgBouncer, batched upsert, CDN headers, version cache)
estimated_effort.priority_3: 1-2 weeks (materialized view, search engine, partitioning, read replicas)

verification_checklist: Load test GET /models?category=coding&lang=es at 10k models: p95 < 200ms
Load test GET /models?q=claude at 10k models: p95 < 100ms
Verify query count = 1 for list endpoint (EXPLAIN ANALYZE)
Verify keyset pagination latency constant at page 500
Verify cache hit rate > 90% on public endpoints under load
Verify CDN cache purge on model approval < 5s globally
